title: HEAMS: Holistic Evaluation of Agent Memory Systems
abstract: arXiv:2611.20144v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Memory systems allow AI agents to persist information across interactions, making them more personalized and more capable on long-horizon tasks. This persistence introduces new risks: stored information can be disclosed in inappropriate contexts, resist correction or deletion, be retained beyond what users desire, or be poisoned to influence later agent behaviour. Yet memory systems are typically evaluated on task performance and efficiency alone. We argue that a memory system should instead be understood as the custodian of its user's persistent information, with responsibilities that extend beyond helping an agent complete its tasks, and that it should be evaluated holistically against all such responsibilities. We present Holistic Evaluation of Agent Memory Systems (HEAMS), an open-source framework for evaluating agent memory systems in this way. translated_title: HEAMS：智能体记忆系统的全面评估
translated_abstract: 记忆系统使AI智能体能够在多次交互中持久化信息，从而使其更具个性化，并在长时程任务上表现得更有能力。这种持久性带来了新的风险：存储的信息可能在不当的情境中被泄露、抵制更正或删除、被保留的时间超出用户意愿，或被投毒以影响智能体后续的行为。然而，记忆系统通常仅在任务性能和效率方面进行评估。我们认为，记忆系统应当被理解为用户持久信息的管理者，其责任超越了帮助智能体完成任务的范畴，并且应该针对所有这些责任进行整体评估。我们提出了智能体记忆系统全面评估框架（HEAMS），这是一个以这种方式评估智能体记忆系统的开源框架。首先，我们将智能体记忆系统的职责表述为明确的行为设计要求……（摘要在此处被截断）
tldr: 该论文提出HEAMS开源评估框架，将智能体记忆系统视为用户持久信息的管理者，主张从隐私保护、可更正性、数据保留和抗投毒等超越任务性能的全面责任角度对其进行整体评估。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces HEAMS, an open-source framework that evaluates agent memory systems holistically as custodians of users' persistent information, assessing responsibilities beyond task performance such as privacy, correctability, retention, and poison resistance.
